pure-announcement.rationale: It is MDN reference documentation for a long-standing web standard, not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: Nothing in the supplied nearest concepts (MCP notes, context layer, research sandbox) covers server-sent events or HTTP server push.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The mechanism is specified in the WHATWG HTML standard the page links to and is directly testable in any browser.

durability.rationale: SSE's core mechanism — the server pushes events+data to the page over HTTP via the EventSource interface — is a stable web standard, even though the page's polyfill and jQuery-plugin list is dated.

actionability.rationale: The captured page is a landing stub that names EventSource and defers all usage guidance to a linked article, so a reader cannot build or make a WebSockets-vs-SSE decision from what is here.

atomicity.rationale: The single idea — server-initiated push messages treated as DOM events on the page — is stated in one paragraph.
